column1: # One row per SINGLE run (no medians). lean-align f465a57 against minibwa c07de5c, 4 threads on 4 cores. make_figs.py reads this file for figs/vs_minibwa* and picks up extra rows (new rep numbers, new sizes) without edits.

# experiment gz5m: 5M pairs from gz files, Testing/ec2/run.sh (bench.py), raw rows from Testing/results/ec2_check/{nova5m,hiseq5m}/timing.tsv: wall incl. index load, cpu incl. both gzips. Gbp_hr = Gbp / wall, Gbp_core_hr = Gbp / cpu.

# experiment stream: streamed from the network, no file on disk (NovaSeq HG002 30x 10/20/40M pairs; HiSeq GIAB D1_S1_L001 whole lane 33,916,091 pairs). Values copied from runs.tsv (see its header and README for what cpu_s and the rates mean per source).
# NOT included: the minibwa NovaSeq 10M streamed run (742.8 s) because its wall time includes a 158.9 s cold index load. The lean-align 'before' builds are not in this file.

# experiment stream: NovaSeq, the FIRST 10M pairs (3.020 Gbp), 3 runs per tool, SAME pipeline for both tools (resuming downloader, gunzip, cat > /dev/null sink, index pre-cached, alternating runs), 4 threads. From S-P, branch bench/stream-results (Testing/results/stream/runs/n10000000_{ours,minibwa}_rep{1,2,3}/result.json). wall_s includes the index load; cpu_s = aligner CPU only (gunzip/curl not included).

# experiment stream_single: the older single streamed runs (NovaSeq 10/20/40M with md5 or /dev/null sinks and different downloaders; the HiSeq lane for both tools). make_figs.py plots experiment 'stream' where a data set has rows of it and falls back to stream_single otherwise (today: HiSeq).

# experiment gz5m: 5M pairs from gz files, timing box, Testing/ec2/bench.py, 4 threads, default pipes, the SAME sink for all tools, one session, 3 reps alternating; cpu includes both gzips; verify.sh steps 1-5 passed on cc26db2. lean-align cc26db2 and minibwa c07de5c. gz5m_prev_build = the same session's lean-align f465a57 reference rows. gz5m_old_session = the earlier ec2_check session (different minibwa sink).

# experiment stream (NovaSeq): the newest session, S-P, ONE container, first 10M pairs (3.020 Gbp), 4 threads, same pipeline for all tools; lean-align cc26db2 and minibwa c07de5c. stream_prev_build = the same session's lean-align f465a57 rows. stream_old_session = last night's NovaSeq stream repetitions (f465a57). HiSeq stream rows are still last night's (restart caveat) until the new ones arrive.

# experiment stream (HiSeq): the newest session, S-P, ONE container 09:46-11:15 UTC, first 10M pairs (4.964 Gbp), 4 threads, same pipeline for all tools; lean-align cc26db2 and minibwa c07de5c; stream_prev_build = the same session's f465a57 rows; stream_old_session = last night's HiSeq reps. In this FIRST series the two f465a57 references were 237.3 and 213.0 s (11% apart) and cc26db2 225.7-233.3 s (means +1.5% wall, +0.0% CPU): no gain separable from noise. The clean alternating A/B (experiment stream_ab, 6 pairs) supersedes it: on streamed HiSeq there is no measurable difference between the builds, within about +/-3%; no regression is shown.

# experiment stream_ab (HiSeq, not plotted in vs_minibwa): the clean A/B, S-P, one container, first 10M HiSeq pairs (4.964 Gbp), 4 threads, strictly alternating new (cc26db2) / old (f465a57) after one discarded warm-up, no minibwa; rep = pair number 1..6. Paired differences new - old: wall median -8.2 s (range -16.2 to +10.0; new faster in 4 of 6), aligner CPU median -34.0 s (range -62.0 to +24.5; new lower in 5 of 6); means wall 225.5 vs 231.2 s (-2.5%), CPU 723.4 vs 752.2 s (-3.8%); the container drifted slower during the series (new build's CPU 678 -> 771 s over pairs 1-5); sign test p = 0.69 (wall), 0.22 (CPU).

# experiment gz5m_pipes1MiB (not plotted): the second gz series of the timing box, pipes = 1 MiB for all tools (fix/ec2-pipes be60ea4 bench.py), same builds and method as gz5m (64 KiB pipes); 3 reps; rows from Testing/results/ec2_check/instr_all/pipes_1MiB/timing_{nova5m,hiseq5m}_pipes1MiB.tsv (origin/bench/ec2-check). 1 MiB pipes gave no gain for any tool.
